subject: Prod ingestion forecast + $/1M target (hosted API)
messages:
From: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@heliumhealth.com>
To: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Nov 2028 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Prod ingestion forecast + $/1M target (hosted API)

Hi Jordan / Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo earlier — quick follow-up with the traffic snapshot you asked for (attached). High level:

- Expected monthly token volume: 65,000,000 - 80,000,000 tokens (we're modeling 75M as the central estimate).
- Typical steady-state TPS: ~25-35 TPS.
- Daily peak window: roughly 30–45 minutes where concurrency spikes; observed peak TPS ~220–260 during those windows (short-lived, ~30–45 minutes).
- Prompt mix: ~75% short prompts (10–80 tokens), 25% long-context (400–1,200 tokens) for summarization and extraction.
- Latency sensitivity: <300ms P95 for short prompts; long-context can tolerate higher latency.

Budget target: our finance team would like to keep unit economics at or under $20 / 1M tokens if possible (they flagged $18–20 as the target range). We understand price varies by model and SLA; please advise best fit and estimated $/1M for an initial committed band.

Next steps from our side: attaching a one-week sample of production API traffic (api-traffic-sample.csv). Happy to walk through it live if helpful.

Thanks,
Alex Ruiz
Head of Platform, Helium Health
alex.ruiz@heliumhealth.com

Attachment: api-traffic-sample.csv (CSV, 120KB)

From: Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@heliumhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 1 Nov 2028 18:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prod ingestion forecast + $/1M target (hosted API)

Alex — thanks for the snapshot and the clear targets. A few clarifying items so we can size a clean hosted pricing proposal: 

1) Peak behavior: can you confirm whether the 220–260 TPS spikes are sustained across all endpoints (ingest + summarization) or isolated to a single route? Also, is the 30–45 minute window predictable (daily cron job) or ad hoc?

2) Model family: do you expect to use an LLaMA-style open variant or a higher-accuracy family (we can propose Redwood-verified weights + quantization). Pricing and achievable $/1M differ by model class.

3) Commit flexibility: would Helium Health consider a 6–12 month committed band for step pricing? For example, 50–100M tokens/month committed gives us room to offer a lower unit price and guaranteed capacity for peak TPS.

I attached a mutual action plan template (mutual_action_plan.docx) with proposed milestones (PO, security review, contract signature, onboarding). If you can confirm the three items above, we’ll model both a conservative and an aggressive band and send back two pricing options (no-SLA and basic SLA) plus an option with guaranteed burst capacity for the daily peaks.

Jordan Blake
Senior Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachment: mutual_action_plan.docx (DOCX)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@heliumhealth.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 2 Nov 2028 09:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prod ingestion forecast + $/1M target (hosted API)

Alex / Jordan — looping in pricing details and capacity guidance. Quick notes: 

- If Helium Health is comfortable with an open-model variant (quantized 4-bit), we can approximate $/1M in the $12–16 range with a 12-month commit at 50–100M tokens/mo. That estimate assumes continuous batching and prefix caching for the short prompts.

- For higher-quality families or using larger-context models for extraction, expect $/1M in the $18–26 range depending on average token length and KV cache behavior. The long-context calls (400–1,200 tokens) are the biggest driver of token consumption and compute.

- Peak TPS: to cover 260 TPS sustained for 45 minutes (worst case), we recommend reserving a dedicated burst pool with autoscale headroom; we can model a guaranteed burst SLA for daily windows. That adds a small capacity premium but avoids throttling risk.

I attached a compact pricing-band table to show tiered unit prices and associated capacity reservations. If you confirm model family + a committed band (example options: 50M/mo, 75M/mo, 100M/mo), I’ll produce a formal pricing worksheet with exact $/1M and expected monthly invoice.

Thanks,
Karthik Iyer
Director, Sales Pricing, Redwood Inference

Attachment: pricing-band-table.pdf (PDF)

From: Alex Ruiz <alex.ruiz@heliumhealth.com>

Cc: Priya Singh <priya.singh@heliumhealth.com>
Date: Fri, 3 Nov 2028 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Prod ingestion forecast + $/1M target (hosted API)

Jordan / Karthik — thanks for the quick responses. Confirmations below: 

- Peak behavior: the spike is concentrated on the ingest pipeline (parsing + enrichment) when our nightly batch completes; summarization traffic is more distributed. The 30–45 minute window is predictable and occurs shortly after midnight PT (cron job).
- Model family: we’d like to start on an open variant (quantized) for cost, and evaluate a mid-sized higher-quality model for a second route in Q2.
- Commit: Helium Health can consider a 9–12 month commit at a 75M tokens/mo band for the initial phase if Redwood can hit ~$18–20 / 1M with a burst SLA covering the daily 45-minute window.

Action items: please send a formal two-option quote — (A) 75M/mo commit @ best-effort SLA with unit price target $18 / 1M, and (B) 75M/mo commit + burst SLA for the 45-minute daily window (include burst capacity cost). Also include expected onboarding timeline and draft contract / PO language we should review.

If you want to jump on a 30-minute call to finalize the MAP and timelines, we’re available Mon/Tue next week after 10am PT.

Best,
Alex Ruiz
Head of Platform, Helium Health
